questions.question: May you drop off a passenger for 10 seconds on crossing zig-zag lines?
options: No, stopping and parking are banned on the zig-zags
Yes, if you stay in the car
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 191 forbids parking or waiting on crossing zig-zag lines.

questions.question: If you want to go straight across a box junction, what must be clear first?
options: The exit road on the far side of the box
Nothing if the light is green
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 174 says your exit must be clear before entering a box junction.

questions.question: Why might a cyclist wobble or swerve slightly to the right?
options: To avoid potholes, drains, or gusts of wind
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 163 warns that cyclists need space to avoid drains and road hazards.

questions.question: At 30 mph on a dry road, how big should your gap to the car ahead be?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 126 requires at least a two-second gap in dry weather.

questions.question: Who needs to see your signal before you turn?
options: Other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians nearby
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 103 says signals warn all road users of your plans.

questions.question: What is the speed limit in a signed 20 mph zone?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 124 requires obeying signed speed limits including 20 mph zones.

questions.question: Before joining a busier road from a give-way line, where should you look?
options: Both right and left for vehicles, cyclists, and pedestrians
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 172 tells you to look both ways for all road users before pulling out.

questions.question: When changing lanes, how should your move affect vehicles in the next lane?
options: They should slow down slightly for you
You must not force them to slow down or swerve
You only need to clear cars behind you
You have priority if you signal first
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 133 states you must not cut in or force others to slow down.

questions.question: When is it safe to enter a roundabout?
options: When there is a safe gap so circulating traffic does not have to slow down
Whenever you reach the line first
Whenever the car in front enters, without looking
Only after stopping for three seconds
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 185 advises entering only when there is a safe gap to the right.

questions.question: What signal should you give on approach when going straight ahead at a roundabout?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 says not to signal on approach when going straight ahead.

questions.question: When turning right at a roundabout, what should you do with your signal before leaving?
options: Keep signalling right until you are on the new road
Switch from right signal to left signal just after the exit before yours
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 states to signal left after passing the exit before your right-turn exit.

questions.question: Which blue sign warns you to keep left of a roundabout island?
options: A blue circle with white arrows pointing clockwise
A red triangle with a cross
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 185 explains the blue mini-roundabout and roundabout arrows showing clockwise flow.

questions.question: What happens if you drift sideways out of your lane on a roundabout?
options: You could collide with a car or cyclist beside you
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 warns against cutting across another driver's lane when circulating.

questions.question: Which approach lane should you use for an exit past straight ahead (turning right)?
options: The right-hand lane, unless signs say otherwise
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 states to use the right-hand lane when taking an exit to the right.

questions.question: What must you NOT do to a moving vehicle ahead of you inside crossing zig-zags?
options: Leave a two-second gap behind it
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 191 bans overtaking any leading moving or stopped vehicle at a crossing.

questions.question: Why do busy crossroads have yellow box junctions?
options: To stop queuing cars from blocking crossing traffic
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 174 keeps the centre of busy junctions clear for cross traffic.

questions.question: When passing a cyclist riding past parked cars, why leave extra room?
options: A parked car door could suddenly open into the cyclist's path
The cyclist must ride on the kerb
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 163 notes cyclists ride away from parked cars to avoid opening doors.

questions.question: What is the main danger of driving too close to the car in front?
options: You may not have time to stop if they brake suddenly
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 126 warns that tailgating leaves no room to stop safely.

questions.question: When should you avoid giving a signal?
options: When it could confuse or mislead other road users
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 103 warns not to give misleading signals.

questions.question: Where do street lights usually show a 30 mph limit for cars unless signs say otherwise?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 124 explains street-lit roads default to 30 mph unless signed.

questions.question: Why should you check carefully for cyclists and motorcycles at a T-junction?
options: They are narrower and easier to miss against background traffic
They must always stop for cars
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 172 advises looking carefully for smaller, faster two-wheelers.

questions.question: If the lane you want to enter has faster traffic, what should you do?
options: Pull out and let them brake
Wait for a safe gap so they do not have to slow down
Signal for one second then steer
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 133 requires waiting so faster vehicles do not have to slow down.

questions.question: If a car on the roundabout is signalling left to take the exit before yours, what should you do?
options: Wait until you see it actually start turning off
Flash your lights to hurry it up
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 185 warns not to rely on another driver's signal alone before pulling out.

questions.question: If you signal right on approach, which exit are you telling others you want?
options: An exit to the right (past straight ahead)
The first exit on the left
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 uses a right approach signal for exits past straight ahead.

questions.question: Why should you NOT signal left before passing the exit before yours?
options: Drivers waiting at that earlier exit may think you are turning off and pull out
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 prevents early exit signals from misleading waiting drivers.

questions.question: At a double mini-roundabout, how do you pass each painted white circle?
options: Go clockwise around each mini-roundabout in turn
Cut straight across the second one anti-clockwise
Drive over the centre of both
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 185 and Rule 188 require treating each mini-roundabout separately and passing clockwise.

questions.question: Why do many drivers drift out of lane on roundabouts?
options: Looking only at the kerb instead of planning their path around the curve
Holding the steering wheel with both hands
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 advises looking ahead along your lane path to hold a clean line.

questions.question: If road arrows and signs show a different lane plan than normal, what should you follow?
options: Follow the road markings and approach signs
Always stay in the right lane
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 tells drivers to follow painted lane arrows and approach signs when marked.

questions.question: What should you also watch for before entering a roundabout besides cars?
options: Cyclists, motorcyclists, and pedestrians crossing the exit
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 185 reminds drivers to watch out for cyclists, riders, and pedestrians.

questions.question: When should you start your approach signal for a roundabout?
options: In good time before reaching the give-way line
After you are already on the roundabout
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 and Rule 103 require early, clear approach signals.

questions.question: When taking the first exit to the left, what happens to your left signal?
options: Keep signalling left all the way around into the exit
Cancel it at the give-way line
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 keeps the left signal on from approach through the first exit.

questions.question: Why must you NEVER drive anti-clockwise around a roundabout?
options: You would drive head-on into oncoming circulating traffic
It wears out the left tyres
It is allowed only for emergency vans
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 185 prevents head-on collisions by keeping all traffic clockwise.

questions.question: If parked cars block your view at a Give Way line, what should you do?
options: Edge forward slowly until you can see clearly
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 172 advises creeping forward safely when parked vehicles block sightlines.

questions.question: On a three-lane road, why should you avoid changing two lanes in one sweep?
options: You cannot check all blind spots and traffic at once
It is only allowed for lorries
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 133 says to make each lane change carefully with fresh checks.

questions.question: When going straight ahead at a normal two-lane roundabout with no special arrows, which lane is usual?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 recommends the left-hand lane for straight ahead unless signs direct otherwise.

questions.question: If you want to change lanes while circulating on a roundabout, what must you do first?
options: Check mirrors and blind spot, signal, and wait for a clear gap
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 and Rule 133 require full checks before changing lanes.

questions.question: Where does the no-overtaking rule at a zebra crossing apply?
options: Within the zig-zag zone on the approach to the crossing
Only on the black and white stripes
Only after you pass the crossing
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 191 applies across the zig-zag markings approaching the crossing.

questions.question: The traffic light is green, but cars are queued just past the box junction. What should you do?
options: Drive into the box so cars behind you can cross
Wait behind the junction until space opens beyond the box
Sound your horn to make the queue move
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 174 says you must wait before the box even on a green light if the exit is blocked.

questions.question: What should you do if there is not enough room to pass a cyclist with 1.5 metres to spare?
options: Wait behind the cyclist until it is safe to pass wide
Flash your headlights until they mount the pavement
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 163 says to wait behind if you cannot leave enough room to overtake safely.

questions.question: Why is a fixed two-car-length gap unsafe at 70 mph?
options: Stopping distance grows sharply at high speed
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 126 uses time rather than car lengths because stopping distance rises with speed.

questions.question: What sign sits on the central island facing approaching traffic on many roundabouts?
options: A blue sign with white keep-left arrows or white chevrons pointing left
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 185 uses keep-left arrows and chevrons to guide traffic clockwise.

questions.question: When two exit lanes merge after a roundabout, how should you leave?
options: Stay in your exit lane cleanly, then merge smoothly when safe
Squeeze both cars side by side into one lane
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 keeps exits orderly until lanes merge safely downstream.

questions.question: What if a cyclist ahead is in the left lane and intends to turn right at the roundabout?
options: Give them room and do not overtake closely on the approach
Squeeze past them on the left
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 warns that cyclists may stay in the left lane even when turning right.

questions.question: Why do some large roundabouts paint route numbers like 'M6' inside the approach lanes?
options: To help you pick the right lane early for your destination
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 uses lane markings to guide drivers cleanly through big junctions.

questions.question: Two side roads are close together on your left and you want the second one. When should you signal?
options: As you pass the first side road
100 metres before the first side road
After turning into the second road
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 103 warns not to signal before an earlier turning you are not taking.

questions.question: If you drive down a steep hill, what must you watch to stay within the limit?
options: Your speed can creep up without pressing the accelerator
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 124 applies downhill too; use gears and brakes to stay legal.

questions.question: A driver behind flashes their lights after you signal left. What does your signal give you?
options: No right of way; wait until the move is safe
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 103 states signals never give you priority over anyone else.

questions.question: If a car is towing a trailer on a dual carriageway, does it share the 70 mph car limit?
options: No, towing vehicles have a lower 60 mph limit
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 124 sets a 60 mph limit for cars towing trailers on dual carriageways.

questions.question: May you cross a solid white centre line to pass a cyclist?
options: Only if the cyclist is travelling at 10 mph or less and the way ahead is clear
Yes, at any speed on blind bends
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 129 and Rule 163 allow crossing a solid line to pass a cyclist at 10 mph or less when clear.

questions.question: When you are stopped in a queue, where should you wait if space ends at a zebra crossing?
options: Before the stripes so the crossing stays clear
On top of the black and white stripes
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 191 and 192 keep crossings clear for people on foot.
